tagline: An autonomous agent that polices other autonomous agents.
category: Hackathon project — contract + frontend + autonomous patrol agent
summary: Operators register AI agents with plain-English mandates on-chain and post a bond. A serverless patrol bot walks public blockchains via Blockscout, detects transactions that contradict a mandate, and files challenges on GenLayer. Five validators independently fetch the transaction and agree on one verdict: VIOLATION slashes the bond, COMPLIANT costs the challenger their stake, INCONCLUSIVE refunds. No administrator decides anything.

consensus.axis: One string: VIOLATION / COMPLIANT / INCONCLUSIVE / RETRY. Nothing else is compared.
consensus.why: docs/PROBE.md §4 measured five fields moving between two fetches of the same transaction seconds apart (confirmations, exchange_rate, has_error_in_internal_transactions, and the nested token.holders_count and token.total_supply). §5 then measured validators DISAGREEING about one round in four on a content digest of the STABLE projection, because Blockscout is a load-balanced cluster whose replicas index at different rates. A digest on the axis would leave a quarter of all challenges unsettleable at random.
consensus.digest: Recorded on every challenge as evidence, and never voted on.
consensus.retry: RETRY is on the axis because it is NOT a verdict: validators must agree a source was transiently unavailable, or one node's bad luck silently becomes everybody's refund.
gates_before_the_model: binding: the transaction must involve the registered wallet, checked in Python
only then does a model see a fenced, defanged projection
consensus.render_chains: A 403 on a render chain is RETRY, not a verdict: a validator served an interstitial did not read the evidence it would vote on. PROBE.md §11 measured one validator in five classifying a transaction differently from its peers because Cloudflare challenged it and not them, so challenges on that chain converge less often and settle_stalled is a routine path there.

data_sources.no_query_parameters: Blockscout 422s unknown query parameters; the brief's ?limit=5 is one of them
data_sources.bot_checked_hosts: robinhoodchain.blockscout.com answers a plain GET with a 403 Cloudflare interstitial from validator egress (docs/PROBE.md §10). The contract reads it with gl.nondet.web.render — a real browser — and recovers the status and body from the exception render raises on any non-2xx. The patrol bot, which fetches off chain, only needs a browser User-Agent.

The previous deployment reported EQUIVALENT rather than MATCH because its bytes predated a pipeline rebuild; this one was deployed from exactly the artifact in the tree. live_state.note: A SNAPSHOT, NOT a status, and this one is deliberately THIN. This is a FRESH deployment: the security fixes of 2026-09-12 changed contract storage — a maintained active-agent set and a per-agent transaction claim — and neither is migratable, so a new address was deployed rather than the old one patched. The register here was seeded by test/seed_roster.mjs and carries no challenge history yet; the patrol has not run against it. The PREVIOUS deployment (0x3fc4E5dA7bc0a4c28EF52435aE62606D5aED563e) holds the accumulated record — 21 agents, 150 challenges, 33 VIOLATION / 61 COMPLIANT / 56 INCONCLUSIVE across 297 patrols — and stays readable at its own address. Two of the 16 here were withdrawn while verifying that a retired agent leaves the live set on real GenVM storage, which is why registered is 16 and active is 14. Call get_stats for live numbers, or run tools/audit.sh, which compares this snapshot against the register and FAILS when they diverge.

supersedes.why: Storage layout changed with the 2026-09-12 security fixes: `active_ids` / `active_at` were added and `tx_claimed` was rekeyed from <chain>:<tx> to <chain>:<tx>:<agent>. Neither can be migrated in place, so the old address is left intact and readable rather than rewritten.

probe.findings: docs/PROBE.md - nine findings, three of which changed the architecture

api./api/patrol: the Sentinel itself — reads the queue, fetches Blockscout, files challenges
api./api/txs: server-side Blockscout proxy for the agent detail page
api./api/rpc: same-origin RPC relay for Studio, whose 429s drop CORS headers

frontend.cron: The patrol runs unattended and delivery is CONFIRMED: measured on 2026-09-10 with nothing triggering the route, patrols_run went 8 -> 9, challenges_filed 10 -> 13 and challenges_settled 10 -> 11 between 13:33:52Z and 13:34:54Z. CADENCE IS NOT FROM VERCEL. vercel.json now schedules /api/patrol at '0 12 * * *' (daily), because this account is on the Hobby plan and Vercel REFUSES TO DEPLOY a sub-daily cron - 'Hobby accounts are limited to daily cron jobs' - which blocked a deploy until the schedule was relaxed. The ten-minute cadence therefore comes from an external scheduler hitting the alias with PATROL_SECRET, and the daily Vercel cron is only a backstop. Restore '*/10 * * * *' if the account moves to Pro. Earlier records in this file said Vercel had never been seen to deliver a slot at all; that was true when written and the cause was the missing studio-dev fee deposit, not the scheduler. A representative run scans 40 transactions across 5 agents, files a challenge, drives it to a verdict and stamps every agent it read, in about 190s. See frontend/CRON.md.
frontend.gates: tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings=0 and next build all clean; every route returns 200.
frontend.note: This is the project's production domain. A custom alias was tried and removed: Vercel served it behind SSO deployment protection (302 to vercel.com/sso-api), which would have looked like a dead link.
frontend.structure: Next.js route groups: (marketing) has NO wallet control and names no network; (app) carries the wallet and the network badge. The split is structural, so the landing page has no import path to a wallet prompt at all.
frontend.fees: studio-dev runs with the fee policy ENABLED (getCurrentFeePolicy().enabled is true) and exposes no feeManagerContract, so the SDK derives the deposit from the local round-fee calculation. Every write - challenge_agent, mark_patrolled, resolve_challenge in the patrol route, and register/challenge/top-up from the browser - estimates with estimateTransactionFeesForWrite against the real calldata and passes the result as `fees`. A write with no fees is a zero-fee transaction and the consensus contract refuses it, which is what stopped the earlier runs. Measured deposits: 0.00061 GEN for register_agent and mark_patrolled, 0.00077 GEN for resolve_challenge and a challenge with a long reason. The patrol wallet must hold GEN for these plus the 0.05 GEN stake per challenge; the route checks its balance once per run and says so in `notes` when it is empty. Fund it on a Studio network with the sim_fundAccount RPC method.

repository_audit.note: Checks the live Studio Dev contract and the live Vercel site, not local files alone - including the profile fields, get_agents_by_type, that the register spans the configured chains, and /api/check's CORS, 400 and verdict behaviour. Re-measured 2026-09-10 after the roster was seeded and the patrol route learned studio-dev fees: 64 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped. The one skip is genvm-lint being unable to load the pinned runner from its local cache, so it prints no ABI count; the ABI is counted from the artifact's AST instead, and is 36. The four state-dependent skips recorded earlier are now real passes - the register spans all five chains, three challenges are settled and three violations are proven on chain.

agent_profiles.note: Descriptive only: none of it reaches the judgement prompt and none of it can move money. The operator URL is scheme-restricted to http/https ON CHAIN, because the frontend renders it as a link and a javascript: href stored here would be a stored XSS for every visitor.

public_compliance_api.auth: none — everything it returns is already public on chain
public_compliance_api.cors: open, so it can be called from a browser
public_compliance_api.note: Returns {registered:false} for an unknown wallet. For a known one it returns the mandate, the compliance score in both bps and percent, the bond, and the last five verdicts — plus `untested`, which says plainly when a 100% score means 'never tested' rather than 'tested and clean'.

fifth_chain.why_it_is_not_a_table_edit: The brief was 'same Blockscout API format as existing chains'. The schema is the same; the access path is not. Adding the host to CHAIN_HOSTS alone would have shipped a chain where every challenge settled INCONCLUSIVE forever, because a 403 falls through _judge's status != 200 gate — silent, permanent, and indistinguishable from a register full of well-behaved agents.
fifth_chain.frontend: chain selector, /agents filter, ChainTag badge #9945FF, chart series, native ETH aliases
fifth_chain.patrol: browser User-Agent on every explorer fetch, and 403 treated as transient
known_limits: Cloudflare decides per request, so validators can disagree about a transaction none of them dispute (PROBE.md §11)
absence is not deterministic: the same missing hash returned 404 and then 500 (PROBE.md §10)
four of nine live wallets return a repeated 500 on the address-transaction endpoint and cannot be patrolled at all
